headline: $10,000 in Tesla When It Joined the S&P 500 Would Be About $15,700 Today. An Index Fund Would Have Done Better.
summary: Tesla stock purchased at $695 when it joined the S&P 500 in December 2020 has returned 57% over nearly six years, translating to roughly 8% annually. However, an S&P 500 index fund investment would have grown the same $10,000 to approximately $20,500 (13% annually), significantly outperforming Tesla. Despite the company tripling its revenue and achieving profitability, most of its growth was already priced into the initial valuation, causing the stock's P/E ratio to compress from 900x to 330x earnings.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite impressive revenue growth (tripled since 2020) and profitability improvements, Tesla underperformed the S&P 500 index by a significant margin. The stock's 57% return over six years (8% annually) lagged the index's 105% return (13% annually). The company's high valuation at entry ($695/share, 900x earnings) already priced in future growth, leaving limited upside. Current P/E of 330x and negative free cash flow due to heavy autonomy investments present ongoing valuation concerns.
